routes.description: Establish that Iraq's conduct justified regime removal under a defensible intervention principle and that human reason and solidarity provide moral guidance without divine authority, while religious doctrines can corrupt judgment and political conduct.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the intervention is connected to sufficient humanitarian and security grounds and material consequences, and if secular moral agency is shown adequate while claimed divine authority is shown epistemically unnecessary or capable of licensing harmful conduct.

motionBridge.description: Connect a justified exception to Iraqi sovereignty with an account of moral authority grounded independently of religion and vulnerable to corruption by divine claims.

centralBridges.description: Specify the atrocities, aggression, proliferation concerns, or other conditions under which Iraq could forfeit protection against intervention.
Show that the consequences of removing the regime materially support the claimed humanitarian and security justification despite acknowledged costs.
Explain how objective inquiry, human solidarity, or reciprocal interests can sustain moral judgment without supernatural command.
Demonstrate how particular doctrines or assertions of divine permission can undermine autonomy, excuse cruelty, or obstruct peaceful political judgment.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Support the secular account by distinguishing unresolved natural questions from evidence for a personal moral lawgiver.
Distinguish secular humanism from political systems whose violence cannot be attributed to unbelief alone.

routes.description: Establish that the Iraq invasion lacked a coherent and prudent justification once its foreseeable harms and selective doctrine are considered, and that transcendent moral authority supplies obligations and restraints that secular accounts cannot adequately ground.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if war is shown to require a burden not met by claimed intentions or benefits, and if religious belief is connected to objective obligation, moral formation, or civilizational restraint while major claims of uniquely religious corruption are answered.

motionBridge.description: Connect the presumption against aggressive war with the need for a transcendent source of binding moral obligation and social restraint.

centralBridges.description: Require a coherent principle and sufficiently compelling necessity before the harms of aggressive intervention can be morally authorized.
Account for civilian, strategic, institutional, and geopolitical costs when determining whether the Iraq invasion was defensible.
Explain why moral knowledge, solidarity, or self-interest alone may not create objective duties or secure obedience to them.
Show how religious narratives, atonement, hope, and transcendent accountability can redirect destructive impulses and sustain moral order.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Use experience with failed interventions and selective applications to test confidence in humanitarian-war reasoning.
Test claims about secular moral sufficiency against revolutionary or state persecution explicitly hostile to religion.

sections.title: Iraq: Necessity, Aggression, and Sovereignty
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether Saddam Hussein's conduct crossed a defensible threshold for intervention or whether initiating war remained an unjustified act despite the character of the regime.

sections.title: Iraq: Consequences and the Consistency of Intervention
sections.rationale: The competing accounts of benefits, human and strategic costs, nonproliferation effects, and selective enforcement are necessary to connect the intervention principle to its practical application.

sections.title: Secular and Transcendent Foundations of Moral Authority
sections.rationale: This is the principal clash over whether solidarity, reason, and reciprocal interest can ground binding moral duties or whether objective obligation requires authority beyond humanity.

sections.title: Religious Doctrine: Corruption or Moral Formation
sections.rationale: Disputes over sacrifice, atonement, punishment, divine permission, and religious experience test whether characteristic doctrines cultivate restraint and hope or compromise autonomous moral judgment.

sections.title: Reason, Historical Violence, and Social Consequences
sections.rationale: Scientific explanation and rival interpretations of atheist and religious political violence provide material tests of the broader causal claims linking belief or unbelief to civilization and harm.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Saddam Hussein’s genocidal repression, regional aggression, and declared nuclear ambitions supplied humanitarian and security grounds for forcibly ending his regime.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Removing Saddam produced material gains including prosecution of the ruling family, restoration of the marshlands, and autonomous, democratic, and prosperous Kurdish provinces.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Pressure generated by enforcing disarmament against Iraq induced Libya’s weapons capitulation and helped expose the international A.Q. Khan proliferation network.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: A state may forfeit sovereign protection through genocide, proliferation violations, terrorism, and repeated aggression, and Iraq repeatedly satisfied those intervention conditions.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Human beings possess moral capacities grounded in solidarity, while religion denies that autonomy and preserves primitive explanations despite the availability of better natural accounts.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Vicarious redemption is immoral because another person may assume a debt or penalty but cannot erase the wrongdoer’s guilt or legitimately take away personal responsibility.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Abraham’s required willingness to kill models servile submission, and claims of divine authorization permit torture, cruelty, child abuse, and political violence rather than restraining nihilism.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Ordinary morality arises from evolved solidarity and enlightened reciprocal self-interest, whereas supernatural rewards, punishments, and priestly authority obstruct mature ethical reasoning.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Twentieth-century totalitarian atrocities do not establish that rational secular humanism causes mass killing because fascist and communist systems retained religious institutions, habits, and forms of political worship.

chunk-004:chunk004-c07.proposition: Competing Jewish and Muslim claims of exclusive divine title transform divisible territory into absolute entitlement and empower minorities capable of preventing political settlement.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Experience of warfare and failed humanitarian intervention undermines confidence that launching wars with benevolent intentions will reliably produce good outcomes.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The Iraq invasion joined cavalier militarism to self-righteous idealism, making civilian harm, strategic failure, and eventual disaster foreseeable.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: The invasion imposed immense financial, human, strategic, and moral costs, empowered Iran, and exposed an incoherent and selectively applied doctrine of humanitarian intervention.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Without transcendent authority, atheism supplies no binding reason for moral obedience, while divine order grounds objective morality and individual self-government.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: The Abraham narrative repudiates human sacrifice, while Christianity redirects preexisting destructive impulses and offers hope and atonement for otherwise intolerable guilt.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Knowing moral rules neither explains nor ensures obedience, and unbelief supplies no basis beyond self-interest for calling conduct objectively right except morality borrowed from religion.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Launching an aggressive war is morally and politically different from declining to launch one, so treating intervention and nonintervention as equivalent forms of imperialism is casuistic.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Intelligent design merits fair skeptical discussion because nature's origins and development remain incompletely understood, and suppressing its discussion displays intellectual intolerance.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Human beings on both sides are capable of enormous wickedness, but religious belief has produced more good than harm, and abandoning it threatens civilization.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: The French Terror and Soviet persecution exemplify distinctively atheistic state violence, and portraying the Soviet regime as religious evades its self-conscious hostility to religion.
